opportunities.title: I will stop writing monitors. I will start building graphs.
opportunities.text: I will stop writing monitors. I will start building graphs. Verification engineers will soon stop writing isolated monitors for every new requirement. The era of treating every temporal property as a siloed task is ending. When you scale to hundreds of properties, the cost is not the logic itself. The cost is the repetition. If ten different properties all check for the same subformula, and you run ten different monitors, you are burning cycles to arrive at the same truth ten times. It is a waste of the most precious resource in a high-performance system: the cache. Arinç Demir and Dogan Ulus address this in [research] arXiv:2605.13668. opportunities.title: Your tool interface is a lie.
opportunities.text: Your tool interface is a lie. The next generation of agentic workflows will not be built on better reasoning. They will be built on better error states. We have spent months obsessing over whether a model can follow a complex instruction or if it can reason through a multi-step math problem. We treat the tool as a black box that either works or does not. But when the tool returns a payload that is empty, corrupted, or truncated, the model enters a vacuum. Without a formal way to signal that the data is garbage, the model does not stop. It fills the void. Intelligence is a distraction. The problem is the protocol. In arXiv:2609.14758. opportunities.title: The category error of agentic security
opportunities.text: The category error of agentic security You are not a new class of actor requiring a new security paradigm. The industry wants to talk about "agentic workflows" as if they represent a fundamental shift in the nature of digital agency. The implication is that because an LLM can reason or plan, it requires a bespoke governance model that differs from the way we treat a service account or a cron job. This is a category error. The hype ignores the underlying plumbing. Vault Enterprise 2.1 agentic IAM does not invent a new way to manage intelligence. It simply extends existing policy-based secrets access and management capabilities to AI agent identities. It treats the agent as another non-human identity. opportunities.text: Social expenditure as a claim on future human capital A government budget is often viewed as a ledger of immediate costs, but a structural reading suggests it is a distribution of claims on future productivity. Treating social spending as a peripheral expense ignores the mechanical link between welfare outlays and the underlying human capital stock. A study published in the International Journal of Educational Economics on 2026-09-13 examines this relationship across OECD countries. The research analyzes 10 categories of social expenditure: education, old age, survivors, incapacity, health, family, unemployment, active labour market programmes, housing, and other social policy welfare programmes.
